title: Anthropic Invests $100M to Train 10,000 AI Engineers by 2027
summary:
Technical staff at firms including Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk will undergo simulated deployment drills to bridge the gap between AI prototypes and corporate production. Anthropic is committing $100M to certify 10,000 'Frontier Deployed Engineers' through its new Claude Frontier Academy by the end of 2027. The program includes in-person training and graded practicals followed by a 12 week real world project deployment at organizations such as Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Deloitte, McKinsey and Commonwealth Bank.

The initiative expands the company's footprint in the enterprise sector, where it has already issued over 175,000 certifications across 46,000 organizations. The first professional credentials from the academy are expected in early 2027, and the company says the curriculum replicates the training used for its own internal engineering staff.

HOLY MOLY: Anthropic is now investing $100 million to train 10,000 engineers to deploy Claude inside companies by the end of 2027.

The first cohorts include engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley, Novo Nordisk and Commonwealth Bank.

Companies nominate their strongest engineers, who go through an in-person simulated enterprise deployment and graded practical before spending 12 weeks leading a real Claude deployment inside their own organization.

Anthropic says they will be trained the way its own engineers learn. 

Anthropic already has 175,000+ Claude certifications across 46,000 firms.

The first Frontier Deployed Engineer credentials are expected in early 2027.
